The '''Istragarde Tribunal''' was the arbitration body created by the [[Treaty of the Concord of Istragarde]]. It was designed to hear border, maritime, humanitarian, and jurisdictional disputes created by the postwar order.

== Structure ==

The Tribunal was composed of representatives from five rotating signatory states, selected every six years. Its members were supposed to act neutrally, though later historians and governments often criticized the process as political.

== Powers ==

The Tribunal could hear disputes, issue rulings, accept appeals when new evidence emerged, and recommend sanctions or joint action requests. It could not directly enforce its decisions.

This weakness was deliberate. The postwar powers wanted a common legal forum but did not want a world government with independent military or fiscal authority.

== Reputation ==

The Tribunal's reputation declined as states learned to ignore or exploit its rulings. Its limited authority was exposed by the [[Invasion of Batravalka]], the [[Volgastani Expansionist Doctrine]], and disputes such as the [[Mariposa-Rhovland maritime dispute]] and [[Mariposa-Astoria maritime dispute]], where treaty language produced rulings and mediation but did not permanently settle the crisis.

By the late twentieth century, it was still useful for diplomatic language but weak as an instrument of actual enforcement.
